theses.observation: DGB suffered a sharp intraday decline of -18.86% with a 27.17% range, yet daily quote volume remained relatively low at $542.2k USDT.
theses.evidence: Spot price at 0.00357 USDT, 24h change of -18.864%, quote volume of $542,212.75 USDT, intraday range of 27.1709%.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: The steep percentage loss on modest absolute volume ($542k) signals an illiquid order-book flush rather than heavy institutional liquidation, meaning minor sell flow caused disproportionate price slippage.
theses.mechanism: When passive buy depth dries up during market-wide risk-off periods, localized market sell orders cut through sparse bids rapidly, creating an aggressive price drop without high net capital outflow.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Thin order books work both ways; if broader crypto markets (e.g., BTC) break below key support, further selling could depress DGB price even deeper without a relief bounce.
theses.what_would_confirm_it: Price stabilizing around 0.00357 USDT accompanied by drying sell volume and a swift reclaim of the lower intraday range on expanding buy volume.
theses.why_a_reader_would_care: Helps traders distinguish between genuine institutional distribution and low-liquidity sell stops, preventing panic-selling at local bottoms.

theses.evidence: Intraday price range of 27.1709% with last price at 0.00357 USDT down -18.864% in the 24-hour window.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Extremely wide intraday ranges on red days often represent sell-side exhaustion spikes, where forced stop-loss sweeps clear out weak hands before a consolidation phase.
theses.mechanism: Cascading stop-loss triggers exhaust remaining short-term sellers; once the sell liquidity is fully consumed, the lack of follow-through supply allows price to reclaim lost ground quickly.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Failure to hold local lows leads to downside continuation, turning a potential fakeout into an established lower-high/lower-low trend pattern.

theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Percentage drops can be deceptive; price change relative to quote volume measures order book density rather than underlying asset selling pressure.
